reading.rtitle: Shipment BS-4471 -- nine days late, and not one of them at sea
paras: Forty pallets were prepared at the plant on the third of May, and all forty were ready on the same day. Two containers were loaded in Santos on the fifth, and the ship left on schedule. Eighteen days later, on the twenty-third, the shipment arrived at the port of Savannah, exactly on the date the customer had been given. Up to that point, nothing in this story is unusual, and nothing had gone wrong.

The goods were then held at customs for six days. The reason is printed on the release form, in one line: the product code was missing on the invoice. It is not an unusual reason. Nothing is cleared at that border without a code on every line, and the officer who stopped the container did exactly what the rule says. The container was not opened, nothing was inspected, and no product was rejected. A document was incomplete, and the shipment simply waited.

The customer was promised delivery on the twenty-fourth of May and received the goods on the second of June. Six of those nine days were spent at customs. Two more were lost after the release, because a truck was only assigned two days later. The last day was lost at the end: the first delivery was made to warehouse four, which is not the address written on the order, and the pallets were moved again the next morning.

The invoice template was changed in March, at the same time the freight forwarder was changed, and the product code was left out of the new version. Two other shipments went out in April with the old template and were cleared without any delay. Nobody made the same mistake twice, which is the clearest sign that this is not a people problem. The template was corrected last week, and every invoice is now checked against the order before a container is loaded.

listenings.text: Roberto, it is Dale, from the forwarder, calling early because you are going to want to hear this before your day starts. Your container is sitting at the port and it cannot clear customs. The paperwork is short one thing: the product code is missing on the invoice, on every line. So what I need from you today, and I mean today, is a corrected invoice with the code on each line, sent to me and copied to the broker. If it does not reach me by the end of the day, the container loses its place in the line and it gets moved into storage, and storage is charged by the day, not by the week. One more thing, so you know where you stand. Your other two shipments went out fine. They were cleared without any problem at all, because those invoices were prepared with the codes on them from the beginning. So this is one document, not a pattern. Call me back when you have it.

I want to give you the nine days broken down, because the number on its own is not useful to anybody. Six days at customs. Two days waiting for a truck after the goods were released. And one more day at the very end, because the first delivery was made to the wrong warehouse and everything had to be moved again the following morning. Now, the cause. It was not the border, and it was not the driver. The invoice template was changed in March, at the same time our freight forwarder was changed, and the product code was left out of the new version. Two shipments went out in April on the old template and cleared normally, which is exactly why nobody saw it coming. And I want to say one more thing, because I know what the next question in this room is going to be. Nobody made this mistake twice. When a mistake only happens once per person, it is not a people problem, it is a document problem. The template has been corrected, and from now on every invoice is checked against the order before a container is loaded.
